choices.text: Normal cells import arginine only through mitochondrial citrulline transporters

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recombinant arginase selectively activates CPS-I within malignant hematopoietic cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Leukemic cells shunt arginine into orotic acid through the pyrimidine synthesis pathway

explanation.summary: Many hematologic cancers such as AML and ALL are arginine auxotrophic, so depleting arginine with recombinant arginase starves the tumor.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arginine is nonessential because normal cells can synthesize it. Select cancers, including many hematologic malignancies like AML and ALL, lack key enzymes of the arginine synthesis pathway and are therefore arginine auxotrophic, dependent on external arginine. Recombinant arginase depletes circulating arginine, selectively starving tumor cells while normal cells make their own.

whyWrongByChoice.A: OTC overexpression is not the basis of arginine auxotrophy; the defect is a lack of arginine-synthesizing enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Normal cells are spared because they can synthesize arginine, not because of a special import route.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Recombinant arginase cleaves arginine into ornithine and urea; it has no CPS-I activating action.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Orotic acid derives from carbamoyl phosphate, not arginine, and is unrelated to tumor arginine dependence.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man doubles his daily protein intake for several months as part of a training program. Which of the following changes in hepatic urea cycle regulation is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased concentrations of ornithine transcarbamylase and argininosuccinate lyase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Relocation of urea cycle enzyme activity from hepatocytes to skeletal muscle

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased concentrations of NAG, OTC, argininosuccinate synthetase, and lyase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unchanged enzyme concentrations with reduced N-acetylglutamate production

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppression of CPS-I activity by the increased load of dietary arginine

explanation.summary: High-protein diets raise the concentrations of urea cycle enzymes (and NAG) to handle the greater ammonia load; low-protein diets do the opposite.
explanation.whyCorrect: Different conditions alter the urea cycle. High-protein diets increase the concentrations of urea cycle enzymes to manage the increased ammonia content; specifically NAG, ornithine transcarbamylase, argininosuccinate synthetase, and argininosuccinate lyase have been shown to increase. A low-protein diet causes the opposite effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Enzyme concentrations fall with a low-protein diet, not with increased protein intake.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The urea cycle takes place predominantly in the liver; it does not shift to skeletal muscle.
whyWrongByChoice.D: NAG increases, rather than decreases, with a high-protein diet, and enzyme levels also rise.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Arginine stimulates NAG synthase and therefore increases, not suppresses, CPS-I activity.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A healthy 25-year-old man completes a 12-hour overnight fast. Glucagon is elevated and protein catabolism is occurring in glucagon-responsive tissues, yet his skeletal muscle is not releasing alanine through the glucose-alanine cycle. Which of the following best explains this observation?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Skeletal muscle cannot perform glycolysis while fasting

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skeletal muscle lacks AMP-activated protein kinase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Skeletal muscle exports nitrogen only as glutamine

explanation.summary: Skeletal muscle lacks the glucagon receptor, so the glucose-alanine cycle does not run in muscle during an overnight fast.
explanation.whyCorrect: The glucose-alanine cycle is driven by glucagon-dependent protein catabolism. Because skeletal muscle lacks the glucagon receptor, the cycle would not occur in muscle during an overnight fast, even though protein catabolism proceeds in glucagon-responsive tissues such as the kidneys, intestines, and immune cells that express ALT. Muscle contributes only during vigorous exercise or when nutrient deprivation reaches starvation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Muscle does express ALT; it uses ALT to load nitrogen onto pyruvate during exercise and starvation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glycolysis in muscle is intact; the missing element during an overnight fast is the glucagon signal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Muscle has AMPK, and AMPK activation is precisely what brings muscle into the cycle during starvation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Muscle can transport nitrogen as alanine; it is simply not stimulated to do so by glucagon.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A previously healthy man has gone without food for 3 weeks and is now in starvation. Skeletal muscle is actively contributing alanine to the glucose-alanine cycle, which it did not do during the first night of fasting. Which of the following mechanisms best accounts for this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acquisition of glucagon receptors by myocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rising insulin levels stimulating muscle proteolysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased hepatic expression of alanine aminotransferase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased lactate output through the Cori cycle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Activation of AMP-activated protein kinase in muscle

explanation.summary: When nutrient deprivation progresses to starvation, skeletal muscle joins the glucose-alanine cycle largely through AMPK activation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Skeletal muscle lacks glucagon receptors, so it does not participate in the glucose-alanine cycle during an overnight fast. If nutrient deprivation continues to the point of starvation, skeletal muscle will also contribute to the cycle, largely through AMPK activation rather than a glucagon signal.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Muscle does not acquire glucagon receptors; its entry into the cycle bypasses glucagon via AMPK.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The cycle does not occur when insulin is present; insulin falls, not rises, in starvation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatic ALT converts alanine back to pyruvate but does not explain why muscle begins exporting alanine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The Cori cycle transports lactate without amino acid metabolism and is not the mechanism of alanine release.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman eats a large carbohydrate-rich meal and her plasma insulin rises. Which of the following best describes the activity of the glucose-alanine (Cahill) cycle under this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It does not occur while insulin is present

choices.label: B
choices.text: It runs at its maximal rate to clear dietary nitrogen

choices.label: C
choices.text: It shifts from skeletal muscle to the erythrocytes

choices.label: D
choices.text: It continues but no longer requires ALT activity

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is taken over by a urea cycle in skeletal muscle

explanation.summary: The glucose-alanine cycle is a fasting/exercise pathway and does not occur when insulin is present.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Cahill cycle transports nitrogen from peripheral tissues to the liver on a carbon skeleton that becomes pyruvate for gluconeogenesis. It operates during prolonged intense exercise or fasting/starvation. The cycle does not occur when insulin is present, as in the fed state after a carbohydrate-rich meal.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Insulin signals the fed state, in which the cycle is switched off rather than maximized.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erythrocytes participate in the Cori cycle by releasing lactate; they are not a source of alanine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: ALT is required in both muscle and liver whenever the cycle runs; it cannot proceed without transaminase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The urea cycle is hepatic; skeletal muscle does not synthesize urea.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with cirrhosis is brought in with confusion and asterixis. His blood urea nitrogen is within the reference range, and a resident concludes that his nitrogen handling must be adequate. Which of the following measurements would more reliably reflect the severity of this patient's condition?

explanation.summary: In hepatic encephalopathy, BUN does not reflect severity; serum ammonia, liver enzymes, and clinical signs are more informative.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urea made in the liver is released into blood and excreted by the kidneys, so BUN is easily measured. When urea synthesis is impaired, ammonia accumulates while BUN stays low or unremarkable. This disconnect is a hallmark of hepatic encephalopathy: elevated ammonia drives neurological symptoms, but BUN does not track severity, so serum ammonia, liver enzymes (AST, ALT), and signs such as confusion and asterixis should guide assessment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Creatinine reflects kidney excretory function, not the ammonia burden driving encephalopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urine urea nitrogen, like BUN, depends on urea synthesis and will underestimate nitrogen retention when the liver fails.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bicarbonate tracks acid-base status and does not measure the neurotoxic ammonia load.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glucose does not reflect ammonia accumulation or the severity of hepatic encephalopathy.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with oliguric acute kidney injury has a serum creatinine of 6 mg/dL, a markedly elevated blood urea nitrogen, and an elevated serum ammonia. Which of the following best explains the combination of high BUN and hyperammonemia in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deficiency of a hepatic urea cycle enzyme

choices.label: C
choices.text: Urea is being made but cannot be excreted

choices.label: D
choices.text: Impaired glutamine transport to the liver

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of hepatic arginase by orotic acid

explanation.summary: In kidney failure urea is synthesized normally but not excreted, so BUN is high while ammonia disposal is still blocked.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urea cycle disorders produce a low BUN because urea is not synthesized. In contrast, an elevated BUN can accompany hyperammonemia in kidney failure: urea is being made by the liver but cannot be excreted, which raises BUN and also prevents proper ammonia excretion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A urea cycle enzyme deficiency would yield a low, not high, BUN because urea is not synthesized.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased CPS-I activity would enhance ammonia disposal, not cause hyperammonemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Failure of glutamine delivery does not explain a high BUN; the liver is clearly making urea.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Orotic acid is a product of carbamoyl phosphate spillover in OTC deficiency; it does not inhibit arginase and is unrelated to renal failure.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A geneticist reviews plasma metabolite profiles from infants with six different urea cycle enzyme deficiencies. Which pair of findings is expected in every one of these disorders regardless of the enzyme involved?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elevated citrulline and low argininosuccinic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated BUN and elevated serum glutamine

explanation.summary: All urea cycle enzyme disorders present with hyperammonemia accompanied by increased serum glutamine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Urea cycle disorders have been identified at every enzyme of the cycle with differing prevalence. Whatever the enzyme, all of them present with hyperammonemia accompanied by increased serum glutamine levels (and a low BUN). The specific markers that separate them correspond to the position of the block in the pathway.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Orotic aciduria is unique to OTC deficiency and is absent in the other urea cycle disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.B: High citrulline with low ASA is specific to argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency (citrullinemia).
whyWrongByChoice.C: BUN is low, not elevated, in urea cycle disorders because urea is not synthesized.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Megaloblastic anemia points to hereditary orotic aciduria (UMPS deficiency), and elevated arginine is specific to arginase deficiency.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A 4-day-old boy has hyperammonemia and elevated serum glutamine. Plasma citrulline is undetectable. Based on this result, two urea cycle enzyme deficiencies remain in the differential. Which of the following tests would best distinguish between them?

explanation.summary: Low/absent citrulline narrows the diagnosis to CPS-I or OTC deficiency; urine orotic acid separates them (normal/low in CPS-I, high in OTC).
explanation.whyCorrect: Both CPS-I deficiency and OTC deficiency present with low or absent citrulline because the mitochondrial steps are blocked. Orotic aciduria is the distinguishing factor: in OTC deficiency carbamoyl phosphate accumulates and spills into pyrimidine synthesis, producing high urine orotic acid, whereas in CPS-I deficiency no carbamoyl phosphate is made so orotic acid is normal or low.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ASA distinguishes citrullinemia from argininosuccinic aciduria, both of which have elevated citrulline, not the low-citrulline pair.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Arginine is elevated in arginase deficiency, which is not in this differential.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A CBC separates OTC deficiency from hereditary orotic aciduria (anemia), but it does not distinguish CPS-I from OTC deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glutamine is elevated in all urea cycle disorders and cannot separate two of them.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A newborn boy is diagnosed with ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency. Compared with the other urea cycle enzyme deficiencies, this disorder is more common in males. Which of the following inheritance patterns accounts for this observation?

explanation.summary: OTC deficiency is X-linked recessive, so it is more common in men; all other urea cycle disorders are autosomal recessive.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency is the most common urea cycle disorder and is X-linked recessive, whereas all the other urea cycle enzyme deficiencies are autosomal recessive. Because it is X-linked recessive, OTC deficiency is more common in males.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Autosomal recessive inheritance is the pattern of every other urea cycle disorder and does not produce male predominance.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Urea cycle enzyme deficiencies are not autosomal dominant disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mitochondrial inheritance is maternal and not the pattern of OTC deficiency, even though OTC acts in the mitochondria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: X-linked dominant inheritance would affect females as often or more often; the male predominance reflects recessive X-linkage.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A neonate develops hyperammonemia with elevated serum glutamine. Plasma citrulline and other urea cycle intermediates are low or undetectable, and urine orotic acid is normal. A therapeutic trial of carbamylglutamate produces no improvement in ammonia levels. Which enzyme is most likely deficient?

explanation.summary: CPS-I deficiency mimics NAGS deficiency (low intermediates, no orotic aciduria) but, unlike NAGS deficiency, is non-responsive to carbamylglutamate.
explanation.whyCorrect: CPS-I deficiency resembles NAGS deficiency in that many urea cycle intermediates are low or undetectable and there is no orotic aciduria, because a similar early step is impacted. The basis differs: in NAGS deficiency the enzymes are intact but unstimulated, so the synthetic NAG analog carbamylglutamate restores flux, whereas in CPS-I deficiency the enzyme itself is missing, so the disorder is non-responsive to carbamylglutamate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: NAGS deficiency would respond to carbamylglutamate, which activates CPS-I directly and bypasses the need for endogenous NAG.
whyWrongByChoice.C: OTC deficiency causes low citrulline but is marked by high urine orotic acid, which this infant lacks.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency produces elevated, not undetectable, citrulline.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Arginase deficiency presents later with spasticity and elevated arginine rather than low intermediates.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A child with ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency has marked orotic aciduria. A student asks why the excess carbamoyl phosphate is not simply held in check by the normal regulation of pyrimidine synthesis. Which of the following best explains the overaccumulation of orotic acid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carbamoyl phosphate directly inhibits uridine monophosphate synthase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate allosterically activates CPS-II

choices.label: C
choices.text: It enters the pathway downstream of the UMP feedback control point at CPS-II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Orotic acid is reabsorbed by the kidney and cannot be excreted

choices.label: E
choices.text: N-acetylglutamate stimulates the cytosolic pyrimidine pathway

explanation.summary: Leaked carbamoyl phosphate joins pyrimidine synthesis below the step where UMP feedback-inhibits CPS-II, so it escapes regulation and becomes orotic acid.
explanation.whyCorrect: CPS-I makes carbamoyl phosphate in mitochondria for the urea cycle, while CPS-II makes the same product in the cytoplasm for de novo pyrimidine synthesis. UMP shuts off its own production by negative feedback on CPS-II. In OTC deficiency the unused mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate leaks into the cytosol and enters the pathway below this control point, so it is converted to orotic acid without restraint, causing overaccumulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: UMP synthase is not inhibited by carbamoyl phosphate; it is deficient in hereditary orotic aciduria, a different disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The problem is bypass of CPS-II regulation, not activation of CPS-II.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Orotic acid is excreted, which is precisely why orotic aciduria is detectable in the urine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: NAG allosterically activates the mitochondrial CPS-I of the urea cycle, not the pyrimidine pathway.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A 2-day-old infant with a suspected urea cycle defect is obtunded with a serum ammonia of 1,900 micromol/L. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate intervention to remove the toxic ammonia rapidly?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Alpha-keto acid analogs of essential amino acids

explanation.summary: Immediate treatment of severe hyperammonemia usually entails dialysis to remove ammonia rapidly; the other strategies are adjuncts.
explanation.whyCorrect: When deficiencies compromise the urea cycle, managing hyperammonemia is of paramount importance. Immediate treatment usually entails dialysis to get the toxic ammonia removed rapidly. Protein restriction, keto acid analogs, arginine or citrulline supplements, lactulose, and nitrogen scavengers are additional strategies for ongoing control.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lactulose lowers ammonia by acidifying the colon but works far too slowly to rescue an obtunded neonate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Protein restriction limits future ammonia generation but does not clear the ammonia already present.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Arginine supplements can increase urea production in some cases but are not the rapid removal step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Keto acid analogs reduce nitrogen intake over time; they do not acutely remove ammonia.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A child with a urea cycle disorder is placed on a protein-restricted diet supplemented with alpha-keto acid analogs of the essential amino acids. Which of the following best explains the purpose of these analogs?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They covalently bind glutamine to form urinary derivatives

choices.label: B
choices.text: They act as synthetic N-acetylglutamate analogs activating CPS-I

choices.label: C
choices.text: They acidify the colon through microbial metabolism to trap ammonium

choices.label: D
choices.text: They increase the rate of urea production like arginine supplements

choices.label: E
choices.text: They are transaminated into essential amino acids without adding nitrogen

explanation.summary: Keto acid analogs supply the carbon skeletons of essential amino acids, which transaminases convert to the amino acids without exceeding nitrogen need.
explanation.whyCorrect: Restricting protein reduces the nitrogen load, but essential amino acids are still required. Adding alpha-keto acid analogs of essential amino acids lets transaminase reactions convert them into the needed amino acids using nitrogen already in the body, providing the amino acids without exceeding nitrogen need.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Binding glutamine for excretion is the mechanism of phenylbutyrate (phenylacetate).
whyWrongByChoice.B: Carbamylglutamate is the synthetic NAG analog; keto acids do not activate CPS-I.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Colonic acidification is how lactulose works.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Arginine or citrulline supplements increase the rate of urea production; keto acids reduce nitrogen input instead.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A child with a urea cycle disorder is treated with sodium benzoate as a nitrogen scavenger. Which amino acid does this drug covalently bind to form a derivative that is excreted in the urine?

explanation.summary: Sodium benzoate binds glycine, whereas phenylbutyrate binds glutamine; both derivatives are excreted in urine, bypassing urea.
explanation.whyCorrect: Phenylbutyrate and sodium benzoate are nitrogen scavengers that covalently bind glutamine and glycine, respectively, to make derivatives excreted in the urine, bypassing the need for urea production. Benzoate is activated with CoA and then conjugated to glycine.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Glutamine is the target of phenylbutyrate's active metabolite phenylacetate, not of benzoate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Alanine is a nitrogen transporter in the Cahill cycle but is not conjugated by benzoate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aspartate donates the second nitrogen of urea; it is not a scavenger target.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Arginine is a urea cycle intermediate that may be supplemented, not scavenged.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with cirrhosis and hepatic encephalopathy is prescribed lactulose, an indigestible disaccharide. Which of the following best describes how this agent lowers ammonia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It conjugates ammonia with glycine within hepatocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: It acidifies the colon, trapping ammonium for removal in stool

choices.label: C
choices.text: It activates CPS-I to increase hepatic urea synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is absorbed and binds glutamine for urinary excretion

choices.label: E
choices.text: It inhibits glutaminase in the intestinal epithelium

explanation.summary: Lactulose is metabolized by colonic microbes, acidifying the colon so ammonia is trapped as ammonium and expelled by stimulated bowel movements.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lactulose is an indigestible disaccharide. Microbial metabolism in the colon acidifies the lumen, which traps ammonia as ammonium ions that cannot be absorbed; lactulose also stimulates bowel movement to remove the trapped ammonium.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glycine conjugation is the action of sodium benzoate, not lactulose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lactulose acts in the gut lumen and has no effect on CPS-I or urea synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lactulose is not absorbed; glutamine binding is the mechanism of phenylbutyrate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Its effect is pH-mediated trapping, not enzyme inhibition.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A pharmacology student asks why removing glycine, a nonessential amino acid that the body can synthesize, helps lower ammonia in a patient receiving sodium benzoate. Which of the following best explains the rationale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Glycine is the predominant nitrogen transporter to the liver

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glycine is a direct substrate of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase-I

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replacing the lost glycine consumes nitrogen that would otherwise form urea

choices.label: E
choices.text: Glycine is converted to orotic acid in the cytosol

explanation.summary: Glycine is in constant high demand (e.g., 8 glycines per porphyrin ring of heme), so scavenging it diverts nitrogen into glycine synthesis instead of urea.
explanation.whyCorrect: Glycine is nonessential and used for a plethora of daily needs beyond protein synthesis. A single porphyrin ring for heme requires eight glycines; hemoglobin holds four hemes, RBCs turn over every 180 days, and cytochromes for phase I detoxification and the electron transport chain need heme too. Removing glycine with benzoate results in more nitrogen being used to resynthesize glycine rather than being routed into urea formation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glutamine, not glycine, is the predominant nitrogen transporter; that is the rationale for phenylbutyrate.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CPS-I uses ammonia and CO2, not glycine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glycine has no described inhibitory effect on NAGS; NAGS is stimulated by arginine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Orotic acid derives from carbamoyl phosphate in pyrimidine synthesis, not from glycine.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A hospitalized adult with acute hyperammonemia from decompensated cirrhosis, with no urea cycle enzyme deficiency, is started on an intravenous solution containing 10% sodium benzoate and 10% sodium phenylacetate. Which statement best supports using this combination in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The solution is a synthetic NAG analog that restores CPS-I activation

choices.label: B
choices.text: The solution replaces hepatic urea cycle enzymes lost in cirrhosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: The solution removes ammonia by acidifying the colon like lactulose

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nitrogen scavenging does not require urea and applies beyond urea cycle disorders

choices.label: E
choices.text: Phenylacetate must undergo beta-oxidation before it can bind glutamine

explanation.summary: The IV benzoate/phenylacetate combination disposes of nitrogen without urea, so it is not restricted to urea cycle disorders and can help resolve hepatic encephalopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: This FDA-approved intravenous solution of 10% sodium benzoate and 10% sodium phenylacetate (the active metabolite of phenylbutyrate) is prescribed for acute hyperammonemia. The agents allow nitrogen disposal that does not require urea while increasing nitrogen demand for amino acid biosynthesis, curtailing catabolism. Because of this utility they are not exclusively restricted to urea cycle disorders and can be part of a combinatorial approach to hepatic encephalopathy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carbamylglutamate is the NAG analog; benzoate and phenylacetate scavenge glycine and glutamine instead.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nitrogen scavengers provide an alternative excretion route; they do not replace enzymes.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Colonic acidification is lactulose's mechanism; these agents form urinary conjugates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Phenylbutyrate requires beta-oxidation to phenylacetate; phenylacetate itself is already the active metabolite.

questions.topicName: Amino Acid Metabolism I: Nitrogen Balance and Urea Cycle

questions.stem: A 2-day-old term female is feeding well but her urine has a distinct sweet, burnt-sugar odor noted by nursing staff. The newborn screen shows markedly elevated leucine, isoleucine, and valine. The parents are given a specialized formula lacking branched-chain amino acids. A deficiency in which of the following enzymes is the most likely cause of this presentation?

explanation.summary: Maple syrup urine disease results from deficient branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase.
explanation.whyCorrect: The sweet, burnt-sugar urine odor and elevated valine, leucine, and isoleucine are classic for maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). MSUD is caused by deficiency of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase, a TPP-dependent complex that oxidatively decarboxylates the BCAA-derived alpha-keto acids. The block causes accumulation of toxic alpha-keto acids that are excreted in the urine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes PKU, which gives a musty odor and elevated phenylalanine, not elevated BCAAs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Homogentisate oxidase deficiency causes alkaptonuria with dark urine, not sweet-smelling urine or elevated BCAAs.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency causes homocystinuria with elevated homocysteine, not a maple-syrup odor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency causes propionic acidemia; while an organic acidemia, it does not produce the maple-syrup odor or the specific BCAA elevation of MSUD.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 3-day-old newborn becomes lethargic and hypotonic before discharge. Laboratory studies show a high anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia, and organic aciduria, with no urea cycle intermediates above normal. Based on the identity of the accumulating organic acid, the physician prescribes adenosyl-cobalamin. Catabolism of which of the following is defective in this patient?

explanation.summary: Methylmalonic acidemia is a methylmalonyl-CoA mutase defect that impairs catabolism of several amino acids including threonine.
explanation.whyCorrect: The response to adenosyl-cobalamin identifies a defect in methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, the vitamin B12 (adenosyl-cobalamin)-dependent enzyme. This blocks the conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA and impairs catabolism of methionine, threonine, isoleucine, and valine, causing methylmalonic acidemia with high anion gap acidosis and hyperammonemia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Phenylalanine catabolism is disrupted in PKU (phenylalanine hydroxylase), which does not respond to cobalamin.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Leucine catabolism is blocked in isovaleric acidemia (isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase), which does not use adenosyl-cobalamin.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homocysteine metabolism is affected in homocystinuria, treated with B6 or B12 for methionine synthase, not adenosyl-cobalamin for a mutase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tyrosine catabolism is blocked in alkaptonuria, which causes dark urine and arthritis, not this acute acidosis.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy has developmental delay and poor school performance. On examination he is tall and thin with disproportionately long limbs and fingers. Laboratory studies reveal elevated plasma homocysteine, and urinalysis is unremarkable for organic acids and ketones. Genetic testing identifies a mutation in the CBS gene. Supplementation with which vitamin is most likely to be therapeutically beneficial?

explanation.summary: Cystathionine beta-synthase is PLP-dependent, so pyridoxine (B6) can rescue responsive homocystinuria variants.
explanation.whyCorrect: A CBS mutation causes homocystinuria. Cystathionine beta-synthase requires pyridoxal phosphate (PLP), the active form of vitamin B6, and some patients respond to high-dose B6 supplementation. The tall marfanoid habitus with long limbs, cognitive issues, and elevated homocysteine fit CBS deficiency.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Thiamine (TPP) is the cofactor for the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase in MSUD, not for CBS.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Biotin is the cofactor for propionyl-CoA carboxylase, not CBS.
whyWrongByChoice.D: B12 (methylcobalamin) supports methionine synthase; it is used when the homocystinuria is due to methionine synthase deficiency, not a CBS mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: BH4 is the cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase in PKU, unrelated to CBS.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man is evaluated for progressive back and hip pain. His wife notes that his urine turns dark, almost black, after sitting in the toilet bowl, and his sclerae and ear cartilage have a bluish-black discoloration. Which enzyme deficiency best explains these findings?

explanation.summary: Alkaptonuria is a homogentisate oxidase deficiency causing homogentisic acid accumulation, ochronosis, and dark urine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alkaptonuria results from deficient homogentisate oxidase in the tyrosine catabolic pathway. Homogentisic acid accumulates and spontaneously oxidizes and polymerizes into a dark pigment, causing urine that darkens on air exposure, bluish-black connective tissue pigmentation (ochronosis), and early-onset arthritis of the spine, hips, and knees.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tyrosinase deficiency causes albinism with hypopigmentation, not dark pigment deposition.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency causes PKU with a musty odor, not dark urine or ochronosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase deficiency causes methylmalonic acidemia with acute acidosis in infancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency causes isovaleric acidemia with a sweaty-feet odor.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A newborn with untreated classic PKU is noted to have very fair skin, blond hair, and light-colored eyes compared with the parents. This hypopigmentation is best explained by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of melanocytes in the skin

choices.label: C
choices.text: A primary mutation in the tyrosinase gene

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excess homogentisic acid deposition in skin

explanation.summary: In PKU, blocked phenylalanine-to-tyrosine conversion limits tyrosine, the precursor for melanin, causing hypopigmentation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Phenylalanine hydroxylase converts phenylalanine to tyrosine. When PAH is deficient, tyrosine becomes essential and is relatively deficient. Since tyrosine is the substrate for melanin synthesis, PKU patients characteristically show hypopigmentation of skin, hair, and eyes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: PKU patients retain melanocytes; the problem is a lack of substrate, not absent pigment cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A primary tyrosinase mutation causes albinism, a separate disorder, not PKU-related hypopigmentation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homogentisic acid deposition causes the dark pigmentation of alkaptonuria, the opposite of hypopigmentation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Dopamine beta-hydroxylase makes norepinephrine and is unrelated to melanin pigmentation.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 4-day-old infant presents with poor feeding, vomiting, hypotonia, and a sweaty-feet odor. Metabolic workup shows accumulation of isovaleryl-glycine and hydroxy-isovaleric acid. A deficiency in which enzyme, acting on which amino acid pathway, best explains this presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase in the leucine pathway

choices.label: B
choices.text: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase in the valine pathway

choices.label: C
choices.text: Branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase in all three BCAAs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Homogentisate oxidase in the tyrosine pathway

choices.label: E
choices.text: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase in the methionine pathway

explanation.summary: Isovaleric acidemia is a deficiency of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase in leucine catabolism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Isovaleric acidemia is a defect in the leucine catabolism pathway caused by deficient isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase, a mitochondrial FAD-dependent flavoenzyme that converts isovaleryl-CoA to 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA. Accumulated isovaleryl-CoA yields measurable derivatives such as isovaleryl-glycine and hydroxy-isovaleric acid, and produces the characteristic sweaty-feet odor.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency causes propionic acidemia with propionyl-CoA buildup, not isovaleryl derivatives.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase deficiency causes MSUD affecting all three BCAAs, with a maple-syrup odor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homogentisate oxidase acts in tyrosine catabolism (alkaptonuria), unrelated to a sweaty-feet odor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase deficiency causes methylmalonic acidemia, not isovaleryl-glycine accumulation.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man presents with severe, radiating right flank pain. Urinalysis shows hexagonal crystals, and a stone analysis confirms cystine. His disease is caused by a defect in the transporter that reabsorbs cystine along with which other group of amino acids?

explanation.summary: Cystinuria is a defect in the basic amino acid transporter that also carries the cystine dimer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cystinuria results from a defect in the basic amino acid transporter (encoded by SLC3A1 or SLC7A9), which also recognizes the disulfide-linked cysteine dimer, cystine. Affected patients cannot reabsorb ornithine, arginine, lysine, and cystine, and cystine precipitates into hexagonal kidney stones, especially in acidic urine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Branched-chain amino acids are handled by the L system and are not the defective transporter in cystinuria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The neutral amino acid transporter (SLC6A19) is defective in Hartnup disease, not cystinuria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anionic amino acids use the XAG- system, which is not involved in cystinuria.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Aromatic amino acids are transported by the L system and are not the group lost with cystine in cystinuria.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 5-year-old child with intermittent ataxia develops a photosensitive, pellagra-like skin rash during a period of poor diet and increased sun exposure. Urinalysis shows increased excretion of neutral amino acids including tryptophan. Which of the following best explains the pellagra-like features?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Loss of tryptophan reduces nicotinamide (niacin) production

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess phenylalanine displaces tryptophan at the blood-brain barrier

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cystine precipitates in the renal tubules

choices.label: D
choices.text: Homogentisic acid polymerizes in connective tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Branched-chain alpha-keto acids inhibit the TCA cycle

explanation.summary: Hartnup disease causes neutral aminoaciduria; tryptophan loss impairs niacin synthesis and can produce pellagra.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hartnup disease is a defect in the neutral amino acid transporter (SLC6A19) causing neutral hyperaminoaciduria. Poor absorption combined with urinary loss of tryptophan reduces nicotinamide production, and when triggered by dietary changes or sun exposure can lead to pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia).

whyWrongByChoice.B: Phenylalanine displacing tryptophan at the blood-brain barrier is a mechanism in PKU affecting serotonin, not the cause of the Hartnup skin rash.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cystine precipitation causes kidney stones in cystinuria, not a pellagra-like rash.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homogentisic acid polymerization causes ochronosis in alkaptonuria, unrelated to pellagra.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Branched-chain alpha-keto acids inhibiting the TCA cycle relate to organic acidemias like MSUD, not Hartnup dermatitis.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: An infant is diagnosed with a severe, rare form of PKU that does not improve with strict phenylalanine restriction alone. Testing reveals a mutation in dihydropteridine reductase. Beyond a low-phenylalanine diet, why is this form more severe and require neurotransmitter precursor supplementation such as L-Dopa and 5-HTP?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Excess methionine accumulates and is neurotoxic

explanation.summary: Malignant PKU results from failed BH4 recycling, which cripples multiple BH4-dependent hydroxylases.
explanation.whyCorrect: Dihydropteridine reductase is needed to regenerate tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). Without recycling, all BH4-dependent hydroxylases are impaired: not only phenylalanine hydroxylase but also tyrosine hydroxylase (dopamine, then norepinephrine and epinephrine) and tryptophan hydroxylase (serotonin). Because diet alone cannot restore these neurotransmitters, precursors such as L-Dopa and 5-HTP are supplemented.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Complete absence of PAH is classic PKU, which responds to phenylalanine restriction and does not by itself deplete dopamine and serotonin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tyrosinase (albinism) is not the affected enzyme in malignant PKU.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Aspartame is a phenylalanine source to avoid, not an enzyme inhibitor causing this severity.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Methionine accumulation relates to homocystinuria, not malignant PKU.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A neonate with propionic acidemia is stabilized. As part of long-term management the team plans a therapy that helps clear the accumulating toxic acid by conjugation. Which supplement is used, and by what mechanism does it help?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carnitine, which conjugates propionic acid to aid its excretion and free up CoA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Biotin, which directly degrades propionyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tetrahydrobiopterin, which restores propionyl-CoA carboxylase activity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thiamine, which serves as the cofactor for propionyl-CoA carboxylase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adenosyl-cobalamin, which is the cofactor for propionyl-CoA carboxylase

explanation.summary: Carnitine supplementation conjugates accumulating propionic acid to aid excretion and regenerate free CoA.
explanation.whyCorrect: In propionyl-CoA carboxylase deficiency, propionyl-CoA and propionic acid accumulate. Carnitine supplementation allows carnitine acyltransferase to conjugate carnitine to the excess acid, freeing up needed CoA and making the propionic acid more readily excreted, analogous to the handling of medium-chain acyl-CoAs in MCAD.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Biotin is the natural cofactor for propionyl-CoA carboxylase, but it does not directly degrade propionyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BH4 is the PAH cofactor in PKU, not relevant to propionyl-CoA carboxylase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thiamine (TPP) is the cofactor for the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase, not propionyl-CoA carboxylase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adenosyl-cobalamin is the cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, the next step, not propionyl-CoA carboxylase, whose cofactor is biotin.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: During the newborn period, several inborn errors that cause accumulation of organic acids present with a characteristic laboratory triad when untreated. Which of the following combinations is most typical of these organic acidemias?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Normal anion gap acidosis, hypoammonemia, and alkalosis

choices.label: B
choices.text: High anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia, and ketosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Respiratory alkalosis, hypoglycemia, and hyperkalemia only

choices.label: E
choices.text: High anion gap acidosis with low ammonia and no ketosis

explanation.summary: Untreated organic acidemias classically present with high anion gap metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia, and ketosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Organic acidemias accumulate toxic acids that, along with ketosis from decreased energy yield of amino acid catabolism and inhibition of TCA cycle enzymes, cause high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The organic acids also inhibit urea cycle enzymes (notably NAG synthase), producing hyperammonemia. Hypoglycemia may also occur.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Organic acidemias cause a high, not normal, anion gap, and hyperammonemia rather than hypoammonemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The primary disturbance is a high anion gap metabolic acidosis, not respiratory alkalosis; potassium is not the defining feature.
whyWrongByChoice.D: These disorders cause acidosis, not alkalosis, and tend toward hypoglycemia rather than hyperglycemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ammonia is typically elevated and ketosis is usually present, the opposite of this option.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A pregnant woman with poorly controlled PKU consumes a normal, phenylalanine-rich diet throughout gestation. Her fetus is at increased risk of adverse effects even though the fetus may not have inherited PKU. Which of the following congenital findings is most characteristic of this maternal condition?

explanation.summary: Maternal PKU with high phenylalanine causes fetal phenylalanine embryopathy, notably microcephaly and congenital heart defects.
explanation.whyCorrect: When a pregnant woman with PKU consumes excess phenylalanine, transplacental phenylalanine adversely affects fetal development (phenylalanine embryopathy). Characteristic features in the affected newborn include microcephaly and congenital heart defects, even if the child did not inherit PKU.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hexagonal renal calculi are the hallmark of cystinuria, not maternal PKU.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ochronosis of cartilage is seen in alkaptonuria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bluish-black sclerae reflect ochronosis in alkaptonuria, not phenylalanine embryopathy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A sweaty-feet odor characterizes isovaleric acidemia, not maternal PKU effects.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 3-week-old girl has an elevated phenylalanine level on newborn screening, and sequencing confirms mutations in the PAH gene. A monitored trial of sapropterin produces a substantial fall in plasma phenylalanine. Which of the following best characterizes this patient's disorder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Atypical PKU with partial PAH activity

choices.label: B
choices.text: Classic PKU with no detectable PAH activity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Malignant PKU with defective BH4 recycling

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hartnup disease with impaired phenylalanine transport

explanation.summary: Atypical PKU has partial residual PAH activity and is usually responsive to BH4 (sapropterin) supplementation.
explanation.whyCorrect: PKU caused by PAH mutations is classified by the relative functionality of the enzyme. Classic PKU has negligible to no detectable PAH activity, whereas atypical PKU retains partial activity that is usually responsive to supplementation with synthetic tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4, sapropterin), the GTP-derived cofactor required by PAH. A clear drop in phenylalanine with sapropterin identifies a responsive, atypical variant.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Classic PKU has negligible PAH activity, so there is no residual enzyme for BH4 to boost; it is managed with phenylalanine restriction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Malignant PKU is a dihydropteridine reductase mutation, not a PAH mutation, and is far more rare and severe.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phenylalanine embryopathy is a fetal consequence of maternal PKU (microcephaly, heart defects), not a diagnosis based on the infant's PAH genotype.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hartnup disease is a neutral amino acid transporter defect (SLC6A19) causing neutral hyperaminoaciduria, not elevated plasma phenylalanine from a PAH mutation.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: The parents of a 4-year-old boy with classic PKU are reviewing his diet with a dietitian. In addition to limiting overall protein intake, they are told to avoid a specific common food additive. Which of the following should be avoided?

explanation.summary: PKU management requires avoiding phenylalanine-rich compounds such as the artificial sweetener aspartame.
explanation.whyCorrect: Management of PKU relies on phenylalanine restriction through limited protein intake and avoidance of phenylalanine-rich compounds. The artificial sweetener aspartame is a phenylalanine source and must be avoided.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Sucrose is a carbohydrate and contains no phenylalanine; it is not restricted in PKU.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tyrosine supplementation is actually part of the PKU dietary plan because tyrosine becomes an essential amino acid when PAH is deficient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Branched-chain amino acids are restricted in maple syrup urine disease, not PKU.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Odd-chain fatty acids are a concern in propionic and methylmalonic acidemia because they yield propionyl-CoA, not in PKU.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 2-year-old with malignant PKU is receiving L-Dopa supplementation to restore dopamine synthesis. For the dopamine produced to be converted into norepinephrine, which of the following is required?

explanation.summary: The conversion of dopamine to norepinephrine requires Cu2+ and vitamin C.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the tyrosine-derived catecholamine pathway, tyrosine is hydroxylated to dopa (requires BH4), dopa is decarboxylated to dopamine (requires PLP), dopamine is converted to norepinephrine (requires Cu2+ and vitamin C), and norepinephrine is methylated to epinephrine (requires SAM). L-Dopa bypasses the BH4-dependent step in malignant PKU, but the downstream steps still need their own cofactors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BH4 is required for the tyrosine hydroxylase step (tyrosine to dopa), which is the step L-Dopa bypasses in malignant PKU.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PLP is required for the decarboxylation of dopa to dopamine, one step upstream of norepinephrine formation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: SAM is the methyl donor for converting norepinephrine to epinephrine, one step downstream.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TPP is the cofactor for the branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase and is not involved in catecholamine synthesis.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: An infant is diagnosed with malignant PKU. The enzyme that is mutated in this disorder normally catalyzes which of the following reactions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: De novo biosynthesis of tetrahydrobiopterin from GTP

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydroxylation of phenylalanine to tyrosine using O2 and BH4

choices.label: C
choices.text: BH4-dependent hydroxylation of tyrosine to dopa

choices.label: D
choices.text: NADH-dependent reduction of dihydrobiopterin (BH2) to BH4

choices.label: E
choices.text: TPP-dependent oxidative decarboxylation of alpha-keto acids

explanation.summary: Dihydropteridine reductase recycles BH4 by reducing quinonoid dihydrobiopterin with NADH.
explanation.whyCorrect: Malignant PKU is a mutation in dihydropteridine reductase, which is required to properly recycle the BH4 cofactor. When PAH hydroxylates phenylalanine, BH4 is oxidized to quinonoid dihydrobiopterin (BH2); dihydropteridine reductase uses NADH + H+ to reduce BH2 back to BH4 so the cofactor can be reused by PAH and the other BH4-dependent hydroxylases.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BH4 is synthesized de novo from GTP by a separate biosynthetic route; dihydropteridine reductase recycles, rather than synthesizes, the cofactor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Phenylalanine hydroxylation is catalyzed by PAH, the enzyme deficient in classic and atypical PKU.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tyrosine hydroxylation to dopa is catalyzed by tyrosine hydroxylase, which uses BH4 but is not the mutated enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TPP-dependent oxidative decarboxylation of alpha-keto acids is the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase reaction deficient in MSUD.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man with classic PKU stopped following his diet several years ago. He now has mood swings and difficulty with gait, and his cerebrospinal fluid shows reduced serotonin metabolites. His BH4 recycling is intact. Which of the following best explains the reduced serotonin production?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failure of dihydropteridine reductase to regenerate BH4

choices.label: B
choices.text: Urinary and intestinal loss of tryptophan via SLC6A19

choices.label: C
choices.text: Consumption of tryptophan by a serotonin-secreting tumor

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lack of pyridoxal phosphate for dopa decarboxylase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Phenylalanine displacing tryptophan at the blood-brain barrier transporter

explanation.summary: Excess phenylalanine competitively inhibits the large neutral amino acid transporter at the blood-brain barrier, limiting tryptophan entry and serotonin synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: In all types of untreated PKU, irrespective of the biochemical basis, high phenylalanine competitively inhibits the large neutral amino acid transporter expressed in the blood-brain barrier. The excess phenylalanine displaces tryptophan transport, which adversely impacts serotonin production and contributes to neurologic and behavioral changes such as mood swings and gait issues.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Failed BH4 regeneration is the mechanism of malignant PKU; the stem specifies classic PKU with intact BH4 recycling.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Tryptophan loss through a defective SLC6A19 neutral amino acid transporter is the mechanism of Hartnup disease, not PKU.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tryptophan depletion by a serotonin-overproducing tumor describes carcinoid tumors, which are not present here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PLP is needed to decarboxylate 5-HTP to serotonin, but PKU does not cause PLP deficiency; the block is at tryptophan entry into the brain.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with a metastatic carcinoid tumor and chronic flushing and diarrhea develops a scaly dermatitis on sun-exposed skin and new confusion. Which of the following best explains these new findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Depletion of tryptophan needed for nicotinamide synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess phenylalanine displacing tryptophan in the brain

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defective renal reabsorption of neutral amino acids

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accumulation of homogentisic acid within the skin

explanation.summary: Carcinoid tumors overproduce serotonin, consuming tryptophan needed for nicotinamide and causing pellagra.
explanation.whyCorrect: The tryptophan hydroxylase pathway that forms 5-HTP and serotonin is upregulated in select tumors like carcinoid tumors. Overproduction of serotonin causes symptoms of serotonin excess and also depletes the tryptophan substrate required for nicotinamide production. This aggressive consumption of tryptophan can lead to pellagra, with dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Phenylalanine displacing tryptophan at the blood-brain barrier is a mechanism in PKU, not carcinoid tumors.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Defective renal reabsorption of neutral amino acids is Hartnup disease; here tryptophan is consumed by the tumor rather than lost in urine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homogentisic acid deposition causes the bluish-black ochronosis of alkaptonuria, not a photosensitive pellagra-like rash.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Tyrosinase deficiency causes albinism with hypopigmentation and sunburn risk, not pellagra with dementia.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl with oculocutaneous albinism is seen for routine follow-up. Her dermatologist recommends rigorous sun protection and regular skin examinations because of an increased risk of sunburn and melanoma. Which of the following best explains why melanoma risk is increased in this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Melanocytes are absent from the epidermis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Melanocytes are present but cannot produce melanin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Homogentisic acid sensitizes the skin to ultraviolet light

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excess phenylalanine accumulates within the skin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cystine precipitates within the dermal tissue

explanation.summary: Albinism is a loss of the pigment-producing pathway within melanocytes, not a loss of the melanocytes themselves.
explanation.whyCorrect: Albinism is most commonly caused by tyrosinase deficiency, which blocks melanin synthesis from tyrosine. The melanocytes remain present but lack protective melanin pigment, so patients have an increased risk of sunburns and skin cancer, especially melanoma, because the pigment-producing cells are still there to undergo malignant transformation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Albinism is explicitly not a loss of pigment-producing cells; melanocytes persist, which is precisely why melanoma remains a risk.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Homogentisic acid accumulates in alkaptonuria and forms dark pigment; it is unrelated to albinism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Phenylalanine accumulation is a feature of PKU, not albinism due to tyrosinase deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cystine precipitation forms kidney stones in cystinuria and has nothing to do with skin cancer risk.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy is evaluated for reduced visual acuity. His skin and hair pigmentation are similar to his siblings. His mother reports that her brother had similar vision problems from early childhood, though his skin was normally pigmented as well. Which of the following is the most likely inheritance pattern of this boy's condition?

explanation.summary: Ocular albinism type 1 is X-linked recessive, occurring almost exclusively in males.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ocular albinism is mainly limited to the eyes, causing vision problems with otherwise normal skin and hair pigment. The most common form, type 1, is inherited by a gene mutation on the X chromosome. It is passed by a carrier mother to her son (X-linked recessive inheritance) and occurs almost exclusively in males, matching the affected maternal uncle and the unaffected carrier mother.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autosomal recessive inheritance describes oculocutaneous albinism (OCA1-OCA7), which reduces skin and hair pigment as well as causing vision problems.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An autosomal dominant pattern would typically show an affected parent; the mother is an unaffected carrier here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: X-linked dominant inheritance would affect the carrier mother; ocular albinism is X-linked recessive.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Mitochondrial inheritance is not described for any form of albinism in this context.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: An infant with pale skin, white-blond hair, and blue eyes is found to have biallelic mutations in OCA1. The enzyme encoded by this gene requires which of the following for its activity?

explanation.summary: OCA1 encodes tyrosinase, a Cu2+-dependent enzyme that converts tyrosine toward dopa and melanins.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oculocutaneous albinism results from a mutation in one of seven genes (OCA1 to OCA7), and OCA1 encodes tyrosinase. Tyrosinase is a Cu2+-dependent enzyme within melanocytes that acts on L-tyrosine in the pathway to dopa and melanins; its deficiency is the most common cause of albinism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BH4 is the cofactor for phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan hydroxylases, not tyrosinase.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PLP is the cofactor for decarboxylation of dopa to dopamine and for cystathionine beta-synthase, not tyrosinase.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TPP is the cofactor for the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase deficient in MSUD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adenosyl-cobalamin is the cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, not tyrosinase.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 6-month-old boy is brought in because his diapers turn brown-black after sitting for a while. He is feeding well, growing normally, and has a normal examination. Urine testing is consistent with homogentisic acid. The parents ask what to expect for their son. Which of the following is the most likely long-term consequence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Metabolic decompensation during the newborn period

choices.label: B
choices.text: Progressive intellectual disability despite normal diet

choices.label: E
choices.text: Early-onset arthritis of the spine, hips, and knees

explanation.summary: Alkaptonuria is fairly benign early in life but causes early-onset arthritis as homogentisic acid pigment deposits in joints.
explanation.whyCorrect: Compared to many inborn errors of amino acid metabolism, AKU is fairly benign until later in life. Over time the homogentisic acid intermediate accumulates, oxidizes, and polymerizes into a dark pigment that deposits in connective tissue (ochronosis) and joints, causing arthritis of the spine, hips, and knees at an earlier age than is typical.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Newborn metabolic decompensation with acidosis characterizes the organic acidemias (MSUD, propionic, methylmalonic, isovaleric), not the relatively benign course of AKU.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Intellectual disability without dietary treatment is a feature of PKU and MSUD, not alkaptonuria.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hexagonal renal calculi are the hallmark of cystinuria, a transporter defect unrelated to homogentisic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A pellagra-like photosensitive dermatitis occurs in Hartnup disease from tryptophan loss.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy with homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency meets with a dietitian. She explains that one amino acid the body normally synthesizes must now be provided by his diet. Which of the following amino acids is she referring to?

explanation.summary: Cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency makes cysteine an essential amino acid.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cystathionine beta-synthase converts homocysteine to cystathionine, which is then converted to cysteine. When the enzyme is deficient, cysteine can no longer be synthesized from homocysteine and becomes an essential amino acid that must be obtained via the diet, while homocysteine accumulates to dangerous levels.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Tyrosine becomes essential in PKU when phenylalanine hydroxylase is deficient, not in CBS deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Methionine is upstream of homocysteine and is already an essential amino acid; the CBS block does not change its status.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serine is not made through the transsulfuration pathway and remains nonessential.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Glycine synthesis does not depend on cystathionine beta-synthase.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 72-year-old woman has fatigue and a macrocytic anemia. Laboratory studies show elevated plasma homocysteine and elevated methylmalonic acid. Antibodies against intrinsic factor are detected. Which of the following best characterizes the cause of her elevated homocysteine?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoimmune malabsorption causing vitamin B12 deficiency

choices.label: E
choices.text: Genetic defect of the basic amino acid transporter

explanation.summary: Elevated homocysteine can arise from acquired B6, folate, or B12 deficiency rather than a genetic enzyme defect.
explanation.whyCorrect: Elevated homocysteine levels can occur from vitamin deficiencies including vitamin B6, folate (B9), and vitamin B12. These arise from dietary, autoimmune, or malabsorption causes, not a genetic deficiency of an enzyme. Anti-intrinsic factor antibodies indicate autoimmune B12 malabsorption; because B12 is needed both by methionine synthase (methyl-B12) and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (adenosyl-cobalamin), both homocysteine and methylmalonic acid rise.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Inherited CBS deficiency presents in childhood with marfanoid features and would not explain a late-onset picture with intrinsic factor antibodies and elevated MMA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A genetic methionine synthase defect would raise homocysteine but would not explain elevated methylmalonic acid or the autoimmune antibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Genetic mutase deficiency causes methylmalonic acidemia in the newborn period and does not raise homocysteine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A basic amino acid transporter defect causes cystinuria with kidney stones, unrelated to homocysteine.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A newborn is diagnosed with maple syrup urine disease. The enzyme complex deficient in this patient catalyzes a reaction that is mechanistically most similar to that catalyzed by which of the following?

explanation.summary: The branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase is a TPP-dependent oxidative decarboxylation complex like PDH and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.
explanation.whyCorrect: MSUD is a deficiency of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase, a TPP-dependent enzyme complex that catalyzes oxidative decarboxylation reactions similar to pyruvate dehydrogenase or alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase. The complex releases CO2 and produces NADH while converting the transaminated BCAA alpha-keto acids into their acyl-CoA products.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase is a biotin-dependent carboxylation, adding CO2 rather than removing it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase is an adenosyl-cobalamin-dependent isomerization, not an oxidative decarboxylation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase is an FAD-dependent flavoenzyme dehydrogenation, not a TPP-dependent decarboxylation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cystathionine beta-synthase is a PLP-dependent enzyme in the transsulfuration pathway.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: The parents of a newborn with maple syrup urine disease consent to a trial of vitamin supplementation that the team explains can partially rescue the function of select enzyme variants. Which of the following is the most appropriate supplement?

explanation.summary: The BCAA alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase requires TPP, so aggressive thiamine supplementation can partially rescue select MSUD variants.
explanation.whyCorrect: The branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex requires thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP). Because thiamine is a cofactor for the various complexes of the alpha-keto acid dehydrogenases involved in branched-chain amino acids, aggressive thiamine supplementation can partially rescue function of select enzyme variants, alongside a diet low in isoleucine, leucine, and valine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pyridoxine (PLP) is the vitamin therapy for cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency in homocystinuria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Biotin is the cofactor for propionyl-CoA carboxylase, relevant to propionic acidemia rather than MSUD.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cobalamin derivatives support methionine synthase (methyl-B12) and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (adenosyl-cobalamin), not the BCAA dehydrogenase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sapropterin (BH4) is used for BH4-responsive PKU due to PAH mutations.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A medical student asks why the inability to catabolize branched-chain amino acids in maple syrup urine disease creates such a significant energy imbalance. Which of the following statements best describes the normal role of branched-chain amino acids?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are catabolized exclusively in the liver

choices.label: B
choices.text: They yield only ketone bodies and cannot enter the TCA cycle

choices.label: C
choices.text: They make up less than 5% of the amino acids in proteins

choices.label: D
choices.text: They are reserved for protein synthesis and are never oxidized

choices.label: E
choices.text: They supply about 20% of the ATP in resting skeletal muscle

explanation.summary: BCAAs are a major fuel: nearly all tissues oxidize them, and about 20% of resting skeletal muscle ATP comes from BCAA oxidation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nearly all tissues catabolize BCAAs for energy, as 25% of the amino acids within proteins are BCAAs. In skeletal muscle, approximately 20% of the total ATP supply in a resting muscle comes from BCAA oxidation, and in the brain BCAAs also provide a source of nitrogen for neurotransmitter synthesis during fasting. Blocking their catabolism therefore causes significant energy imbalance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: BCAAs are catabolized by nearly all tissues, not exclusively the liver; skeletal muscle is a major site.
whyWrongByChoice.B: BCAAs can be converted to TCA intermediates such as succinyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA, so they do enter the TCA cycle.
whyWrongByChoice.C: BCAAs constitute about 25% of the amino acids in proteins, a large fraction rather than a minor one.
whyWrongByChoice.D: BCAAs are routinely oxidized for energy in muscle and other tissues.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A previously healthy 16-year-old girl develops vomiting, lethargy, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, and hyperammonemia 2 days after an appendectomy during which she had minimal oral intake. Evaluation reveals a previously undiagnosed mild variant of an organic acidemia. Which of the following most likely precipitated this first episode?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acidic urine pH during the hospitalization

explanation.summary: Milder organic acidemias can first present in adolescence or adulthood when a stressor such as illness, trauma, surgery, or prolonged fasting triggers amino acid catabolism.
explanation.whyCorrect: Milder forms of the organic acidemias exist, and presentation may be delayed until adolescence or adulthood. Some forms require the right stressor to initiate amino acid catabolism, such as illness, trauma, surgery, or prolonged fasting. The resulting rapid decline, called metabolic decompensation, produces severe metabolic acidosis, hyperammonemia, and ketosis, and can be fatal if not quickly recognized.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Increased sun exposure is a trigger for symptomatic Hartnup disease (pellagra), not for organic acidemia decompensation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aspartame is a phenylalanine source that is a concern in PKU, which does not cause a high anion gap acidosis with hyperammonemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dietary tyrosine is not a trigger for organic acidemias; tyrosine is actually supplemented in PKU.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Acidic urine promotes cystine stone precipitation in cystinuria and is unrelated to metabolic decompensation.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: An infant with propionic acidemia is started on a diet that restricts the amino acids whose catabolism produces propionyl-CoA. Which of the following amino acids does NOT need to be restricted on this basis?

explanation.summary: Valine, methionine, isoleucine, and threonine yield propionyl-CoA; leucine is catabolized to acetyl-CoA and acetoacetate instead.
explanation.whyCorrect: The breakdown of valine, methionine, isoleucine, and threonine all result in a propionyl-CoA intermediate, so these four amino acids accumulate toxic propionyl-CoA when propionyl-CoA carboxylase is deficient. Leucine catabolism proceeds through isovaleryl-CoA and HMG-CoA to acetyl-CoA and acetoacetate and does not generate propionyl-CoA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Valine is catabolized through isobutyryl-CoA to propionyl-CoA and must be restricted.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isoleucine is catabolized through 2-methylbutyryl-CoA to propionyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA and must be restricted.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methionine produces propionyl-CoA through a pathway independent of the MSUD enzyme and must be restricted.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Threonine also produces propionyl-CoA upon catabolism and must be restricted.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 4-day-old newborn develops poor feeding, vomiting, hypotonia, hyperammonemia, and metabolic acidosis. Organic acid analysis leads to a diagnosis of propionic acidemia. The enzyme deficient in this patient normally catalyzes which of the following reactions?

choices.label: C
choices.text: ATP- and biotin-dependent carboxylation of propionyl-CoA

explanation.summary: Propionyl-CoA carboxylase uses biotin and ATP to add CO2 to three-carbon propionyl-CoA, forming four-carbon methylmalonyl-CoA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Propionic acidemia is a deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme propionyl-CoA carboxylase. Normally this enzyme carboxylates, adding one carbon in the form of CO2 with ATP consumption, the three-carbon molecule propionyl-CoA, using vitamin B7 (biotin) as a cofactor, to form the four-carbon molecule methylmalonyl-CoA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Isomerization of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA is catalyzed by methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, the enzyme deficient in methylmalonic acidemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: FAD-dependent dehydrogenation of isovaleryl-CoA is the isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase reaction deficient in isovaleric acidemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: TPP-dependent oxidative decarboxylation of the BCAA alpha-keto acids is the reaction deficient in MSUD.
whyWrongByChoice.E: PLP-dependent transamination of valine is the first step of BCAA catabolism and is not the defect in propionic acidemia.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: An infant with methylmalonic acidemia is hospitalized during a metabolic crisis. The nutrition team specifically avoids lipid preparations containing odd-chain fatty acids. Which of the following best explains this precaution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They inhibit the carnitine acyltransferase II enzyme

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are oxidized to homogentisic acid in the liver

choices.label: C
choices.text: They displace tryptophan from the blood-brain barrier transporter

choices.label: D
choices.text: Their breakdown generates propionyl-CoA upstream of the block

choices.label: E
choices.text: They consume adenosyl-cobalamin during intestinal absorption

explanation.summary: Odd-chain fatty acids are broken down to propionyl-CoA, feeding the pathway blocked in propionic and methylmalonic acidemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Catabolism of odd-chain fatty acids and cholesterol, like that of valine, isoleucine, methionine, and threonine, proceeds through propionyl-CoA and methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA. Because odd-chain fatty acids are broken down into propionyl-CoA, feeding these lipids would be detrimental in propionyl-CoA carboxylase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase deficiencies, adding to the accumulating toxic intermediates.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Carnitine acyltransferase II is actually used therapeutically to conjugate carnitine to excess propionic acid; odd-chain fatty acids do not inhibit it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Homogentisic acid derives from tyrosine catabolism in alkaptonuria, not from fatty acid oxidation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Displacement of tryptophan at the blood-brain barrier is a consequence of high phenylalanine in PKU, not fatty acids.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Adenosyl-cobalamin is the mutase cofactor; odd-chain fatty acids do not deplete it during absorption.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy from a region without newborn screening is brought in for seizures and developmental delay. He has very fair skin and hair, and the examiner notes a musty, mousey odor like an uncleaned rodent cage. The odor is most directly due to which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alpha-keto acids of branched-chain amino acids

explanation.summary: The musty or mousey odor of PKU comes from phenylacetate formed from excess phenylalanine.
explanation.whyCorrect: PKU (PAH or dihydropteridine reductase deficiency) is associated with a musty or mousey smell like an uncleaned rodent cage. Although PKU is not classified as an organic acidemia, excess phenylalanine is converted to the odiferous acidic intermediate phenylacetate, which produces the characteristic smell. The fair skin and hair and neurologic findings fit untreated PKU.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Accumulated alpha-keto acids from BCAA transamination cause the maple syrup or burnt sugar odor of MSUD.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Isovaleric acid, from decomposition of isovaleryl-CoA in leucine catabolism, produces the sweaty feet odor of isovaleric acidemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sulfur from cystine gives the rotten egg odor of cystinuria.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homogentisic acid in alkaptonuria produces dark urine and ochronosis rather than a characteristic odor.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man with cystinuria has had three episodes of hexagonal cystine stones. His urine pH is consistently around 5.0. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention to reduce further stone formation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Alkalinizing agents to raise urine pH

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dietary restriction of branched-chain amino acids

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acidifying agents to lower urine pH

explanation.summary: Cystine is less soluble at acidic pH, so alkalinizing the urine helps prevent cystine stone precipitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cystine dimer has decreased water solubility at lower pH conditions; acidic pH promotes precipitation of the dimer into solid stones because protonation of the alpha-carboxylic acids of the amino acid dimer lowers its solubility. Alkalizing agents can be prescribed to increase urine pH and prevent stone formation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: BCAA restriction is the treatment for MSUD; cystinuria involves basic amino acids and cystine, not BCAAs.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vitamin B6 is used for PLP-responsive cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency, not for a transporter defect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Carnitine supplementation is used to conjugate and excrete propionic acid in propionic acidemia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Acidifying the urine would worsen cystine precipitation by further protonating the carboxylic acids.

questions.topicName: Inborn Errors of Amino Acid Metabolism

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl has intermittent ataxia and a photosensitive rash. Urine amino acid analysis shows markedly increased phenylalanine, isoleucine, leucine, threonine, tryptophan, valine, serine, alanine, and tyrosine, with normal lysine, arginine, and ornithine.
